data.narrative:
Specter is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Xerxes Libsch and Philip Clark that has raised $6.8M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 10 private robotics and manufacturing firms alongside one public comparable (277810.KQ), though peer-median triangulation was not feasible given insufficient depth in same-stage and adjacent-stage cohorts.

The stage-progression method was the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($6.8M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $17M. This multiplier reflects observed step-ups in the robotics sector when companies advance from seed funding rounds, though the method assumes Specter's capital efficiency and market traction align with sector norms. Peer-median analysis could not be executed because only one same-stage comparable existed within the robotics manufacturing universe; expanding the filter to adjacent stages or all-sector medians risked introducing methodological noise rather than precision.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $14M (low) to $20M (high), with a median of $17M. This range reflects a ±15% confidence band around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the strength of Specter's product-market fit relative to peers, capital efficiency trajectory, and near-term funding plans—factors that will sharpen valuation precision as additional operational milestones and comparable transactions emerge.
